title: Bidirectional and causal attention
goal:
BERT and GPT use the same self-attention layer. They differ in the mask (Section 3 and Figure 3).

Write `attention(x, Wq, Wk, Wv, causal=False)` for one head. `x` has shape `(T, d_model)` and the weights have shape `(d_model, d)`. Compute `scores = Q K^T / sqrt(d)`. When `causal` is true, position `i` can read only positions `j <= i`. Otherwise every position reads every position. Return `(out, weights)`, where `weights` has shape `(T, T)` and each row sums to 1.
hints: Compute `Q = x @ Wq`, `K = x @ Wk`, `V = x @ Wv`. Divide the scores by `np.sqrt(d)`, where `d` is the width of `Q`.
Build the mask with `np.tril(np.ones((T, T)))`. Put a large negative number such as `-1e9` where the mask is 0, before the softmax.
Subtract the row maximum before you exponentiate, then divide by the row sum.
Zeroing the weights after the softmax leaves rows that don't sum to 1. Mask the scores instead.
